top.title: North Carolina Central narrowly beat Michael Vick, Norfolk State 29-28
top.description: North Carolina Central narrowly beat Michael Vick, Norfolk State 29-28 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . North Carolina Central secured a come-from-behind victory over Michael Vick’s Norfolk State Spartans , 29-28. Norfolk State appeared to be taking control when a Jalyn Daniels touchdown to open the fourth quarter put the Spartans up 28-17. North Carolina Central answered right away. The Eagles put together a seven-play, 75-yard drive that Jones finished with a 7-yard keeper, cutting the deficit to 28-23 with more than 11 minutes left to play. The ending turned on two late fumbles and a missed kick. Gino Addison, who ran for a game-high 174 yards on 18 carries, fumbled, and Norfolk State recovered with 1:27 remaining. Quarterback Deljay Bailey then ran for 13 yards but fumbled it right back to Central. Jones found Wall for the 26-yard touchdown that put the Eagles ahead 29-28 with 27 seconds left. Norfolk State still had a chance. After an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty on North Carolina Central, the Spartans moved into range, and Marco Peery lined up for a 37-yard field goal attempt with four seconds left that missed. Now, Michael Vick continues to look for his first win in the MEAC after losing against DeSean Jackson’s Delaware State Hornets in the Battle Of The Legends last week. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Meanwhile, North Carolina Central, after starting out slowly early in the season, now finds itself in the running for another appearance in the Celebration Bowl and the MEAC Championship. They now prepare to face South Carolina State . The Eagles have yet to beat South Carolina State since Chennis Berry took over the program for a departing Buddy Pough in the 2024 season. top.title: Matt Campbell updates condition of Penn State football legend Jack Ham
top.description: SEATTLE − Legendary Penn State football player and longtime radio broadcaster Jack Ham was in stable condition in the University of Washington Medical Center Saturday evening, Nov. 7, according to university officials, after undergoing a medical emergency here before the Nittany Lions ' game. Ham, 77, was rushed to the hospital an hour or so before Penn State began their eventual 28-25 victory here in Husky Stadium. After the game, head coach Matt Campbell began his press conference by addressing Ham − and the apparent efforts to help him to safety and a hopeful recovery from his an undisclosed medical situation. Campbell singled out longtime radio partner and play-by-play announcer Steve Jones, who apparently was by Ham's side when he fell ill. The Lions (5-4, 2-4 Big Ten) held on to beat Washington with a dramatic save at the end. "Everybody knows that man, this was a gut-wrenching day for Penn State football with Jack Ham,” Campbell said. “Obviously, a really tough situation as we got off the buses here (at the stadium). “First of all, I think we should all know Steve Jones and the heroic effort that he did for somebody he loves dearly. And if it’s not for Steve, you know, and what he did, I don’t know if we would have as good a news as we do right now. And then I want to also thank the University of Washington, their athletic director, their emergency team were incredible. They were outstanding. I think, hopefully, as all of you know, Jack is in stable condition right now, and obviously, the emotion of that." Penn State went on to play their best first half of football of the season in leading the Huskies 28-6 at halftime − before holding off a second-half surge and desperately hanging on. “What I was really proud of our football team, and we talked about a little bit before we went out to the game," Campbell said. "Just the courage of our kids to play with what Jack Ham means to Penn State football, how that guy played the game, how that guy still to this day serves our football program. It was awesome to be able to go win the football game for him and his family, and our thoughts and prayers will continue to be with him on a full recovery.” Penn State officials were not disclosing the nature of Ham's medical issue or any further details yet on his condition. The Johnstown, Pa. native has worked for more than two decades with Jones, the pair calling their 300th game in 2023. Ham was a consensus All-American linebacker at Penn State and the 34th player taken in the 1971 NFL Draft. He would go on to win four Super Bowls with the Pittsburgh Steelers and would be regarded as one of the best linebackers in NFL history with a particular supremacy as a pass defender. Ham was named the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year in 1975 and made eight straight Pro Bowls. Frank Bodani covers Penn State football for the York Daily Record and USA Today Network. BVB jumped out to a 2-0 lead, but let Elversberg back in the game thanks to a Golazo from Noel Futkeu. Thankfully, the visitors could not find an equalizer, despite playing in front of a record away crowd , and Dortmund now can head into the break without any dropped points hanging over their heads. Niko Kovac deployed his troops in a 4-3-3 with Fabio Silva leading the line, Carney Chukwuemeka and Konstantinos Karetsas on the wings, and Joey Veerman, Felix Nmecha, and Jobe Bellingham in midfield. Joane Gadou got the start again, this time as a right-back. Dortmund did a great job shutting down Elversberg in the first half, with the away side only mustering four shot attempts and 0.09 xG. Dortmund’s midfield was suffocating, and the attacking trio looked deadly. Unfortunately, Chukwuemeka suffered a muscle injury and was subbed off in the 34th minute. Elversberg made the game interesting with what was admittedly an amazing goal. top.title: Penn State postgame report card: Grading Nittany Lions vs. Washington
top.description: They sweated it out in the end, but the Nittany Lions were able to pull out a victory over the Washington Huskies 28-25. Carson Hansen and Chase Sowell starred in an electrifying first half display where the Nittany Lions had 303 total yards, more than they ha in Big Ten games this season. Still, there was a worrying comeback attempt that exposed the defensive frailties that occurred pre-bye week. That's why this game wasn't perfect. Still, the Nittany Lions come away with a second straight Big Ten win and is looking like they could potentially contend for bowl eligibility. Here is a look at the postgame report card for the Nittany Lions against Washington. Quarterback: B For some reason, Rocco Becht can never have a complete Big Ten performance. In the first half of the game, Becht was 11 of 17 for 193 yards and 2 touchdowns. His chemistry with both Zay Robinson and Chase Sowell was on point and it allowed the Nittany Lions to score with ease on four of six first half possessions. Then the second half came. He only completed five passes for 47 yards and didn't lead a single scoring drive. Had the Nittany Lions blown this lead, he probably wouldn't have heard the end of it from fans. Still, he did enough to win and did not turn the ball over, albeit with a couple nervy moments sprinkled in. Running Backs: B+ This was more of an efficient rather than an explosive performance by the Penn State running backs. Unlike last week, they were held under 200 yards and it was a similar committee approach. As predicted, Carson Hansen shown early and was the leading rusher for the squad with 119 yards on 14 carries and a 12 yard touchdown. Meanwhile, Cam Wallace had the other rushing touchdown on the day and finished with 56 yards. While not the breakout game of last week, they played a pivotal role in how the blue and white won this game. Receivers and Tight Ends: B+ Where would the Nittany Lions be without the play of Chase Sowell ? Back from injury, Sowell was easily the brightest offensive star for the Nittany Lions on the day. He had four catches for 125 yards and a touchdown as well as several highlight reel catches. Other than that however, there was nothing of note from the rest of the corps, as the next best receiver was Brett Eskildsen with four catches for 36 yards. Still, it's nice to know that a player of Sowell's caliber can carry the weight for a Jekyll and Hyde offense. Defense: C+ Much like with Rocco Becht, it was a tale of two halves for the Penn State defense. After only allowing only 6 points and 114 yards for the entire first half, they gave up 183 and 19 points in the second half. Demond Williams Jr. went from only throwing for 36 yards to 172. They also continue to struggle to contain the running as six running backs for the Huskies combined for 134 yards on the ground. top.title: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - Jordan Farmar
top.description: The Brooklyn Nets have signed, drafted, and traded for players from virtually every state in the US, and much of the wider world beyond the United States. From Alabama to Wyoming, and from Australia to Ukraine, the Nets have a long and distinguished history of turning over every stone to find the talent needed to succeed in the NBA. From their start in the American Basketball Association (ABA) as the New Jersey Americans and New York Nets to their jump to the NBA as the New Jersey Nets right through to today, the organization has cast their net for talent wide since the inception of the ball club. For this installment of our series documenting the provenience of every Nets player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for Brooklyn. Our focus in this article is Jordan Farmar. An alum of UCLA, he was picked up with the 26th overall selection of the 2006 NBA Draft by the Los Angeles Lakers. The Los Angeles, California native played the first 4 seasons of his pro career with Los Angeles, coming to an end when he signed with the Brooklyn Nets in 2010. His stay with the team lasted until he was dealt to the Atlanta Hawks in 2012. During his time suiting up for the Nets, Farmar put up 9.9 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 4.4 assists per game. top.title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 40 - Ryan Bowen (2004-06)
top.description: The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history. To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day. With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover. And for today's article, we will continue with the eighth of eight who wore the No. 40, Ryan Bowen. After ending his college career at Iowa, Bowen was picked up with the 55th overall selection of the 1998 NBA Draft by the Denver Nuggets. The Fort Madison, Iowa native played the first 5 seasons of his NBA career with Denver, coming to an end when he signed with the Houston Rockets in 2004. His stay with the team lasted until he was cut in 2006. During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Bowen wore only jersey No. 40 and put up 1.5 points and 1.2 rebounds per game. top.title: Mike Florio plans to ‘ignore’ Dianna Russini’s reporting at Pro Football Talk until ‘credibility is somehow restored’
top.description: Credit: PFT Live; The Rich Eisen Show All signs are pointing toward Dianna Russini returning to NFL media next week with a new weekly podcast. The question now is what form her content will take. Will Russini attempt to slide back into her role as an insider? Is her plan to continue to break news? And most importantly, will she address her alleged affair with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel? As the leader of one of the most important platforms in the NFL, Mike Florio is pushing publicly for these answers. Florio not only hosts PFT Live for NBC Sports and contributes to Football Night In America , but he also runs Pro Football Talk, the news site that aggregates all of the league’s latest news and rumors in one place and is widely read by fans and industry insiders. In the latest episode of PFT Live , Florio stated that he plans to “ignore” any news from Russini “unless the credibility is somehow restored.” As Florio sees it, the starting point is that Russini must address what happened with Vrabel. Florio noted that so far, Russini’s only two public comments on the matter were both denials. In the initial article that broke the story open at the New York Post , Russini denied she had any relationship with Vrabel. When she resigned from The Athletic, she accused the media of stretching the truth. “If there’s going to be actual reporting as part of this, you’ve gotta have some credibility, or nobody’s going to believe what you say,” Florio said. “Is there going to be an effort to be an insider again? Unless and until we get an explanation that restores credibility… as somebody who aggregates the reports of others, amplifies the reports of others, wants my audience to believe the reporting of others, I’ve gotta believe it first. “And after everything that’s happened, everything we know, I’m not going to be inclined to believe anything. Which means I’m not going to be amplifying anything. I don’t care what the reporting is. Unless and until it’s confirmed by someone who doesn’t have these credibility issues, I’m going to ignore it. Unless the credibility is somehow restored.” Russini appears to be partnering with BetUS on the weekly show, as well as a written column. She reportedly hired a crisis publicist to help with her return. In an internal report at The Athletic released earlier this year , the outlet’s standards editor stated that Russini’s relationship was a “violation” of standards. The editor found multiple instances of improper attribution of information related to Vrabel and his teams, as well as a video interview that called into question how Russini got access to the head coach. After the report was released, Russini gave a statement saying she stood by her reporting . It would be hard to imagine Russini returning to the public eye without addressing the situation in some way, but news writers and commentators like Florio are already making it clear she will have to earn back trust beyond a simple statement. nigeria.title: AMERICA IS NOT NIGERIA: Why Trump’s midterm defeat cannot predict Tinubu’s 2027 fortunes
nigeria.description: By Kayode Akinmade The sweeping defeat suffered by President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the November 3 American midterm elections has predictably provided fresh ammunition for Nigeria’s opposition politicians, who are already attempting to draw parallels between the political fortunes of the American president and those of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. While the comparison may offer an attractive political talking point, it is, at best, superficial and, at worst, a deliberate attempt to transplant the political circumstances of one country into another. There is no doubt that the Republican defeat represents a significant setback for Trump. Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress, delivering a powerful electoral rebuke to the Republican administration and signalling widespread dissatisfaction with some of its policies. The result has opened a new chapter in American politics and raised questions about the direction of Trump’s presidency. However, the critical question is whether the circumstances that produced this outcome in the United States are sufficiently comparable to Nigeria’s political and economic realities to justify the conclusion that Tinubu is destined for a similar electoral fate in 2027. nigeria.title: Countdown to 2027: Edo North is for Oshiomhole
nigeria.description: By Allison Abanum Adams Oshiomhole’s first term has been defined by a deliberate strategy of translating legislative power into tangible federal presence for Edo North. His legislative record includes moving over 10 motions and sponsoring many bills. These are not abstract motions; they are institutional investments that will outlast any single political cycle. On the ground, Oshiomhole constituency interventions have reached all wards in Edo North, a coverage rate that speaks to both reach and intentionality. Oshiomhole has moved from delivering roads to delivering accountability, and Edo North have seen the difference in both bricks and budgets. Beyond infrastructure, his engagement with youth leaders and traditional rulers signals a recognition that representation must be relational, not transactional, a point underscored by his refusal to charge constituents for assistance and his warning against extortion in his name. The political consolidation around Oshiomhole 2027 bid reflects a broader strategic calculation within Edo North. To the people in the rural areas of Edo North, they have risen from service, unity, and discipline: delivery that touches households, reconciliation that silences internal friction, and grassroots organisation that turns intention into votes. The good people of Edo North on their own are moving ward by ward to get support for Oshiomhole. The plough is heavy; the hands must be steady because the furrow ahead is 2027. The message is clear: no retreat, no sideways glance, no nostalgia for old battles in Edo North. A senatorial district that has seen the light and future must now prove it can cultivate it, row by row, ward by ward, state by state, until the harvest of triumph is achieved. Every leader, every member, every supporter keeps eyes on the furrow, not on the noise. So, let the word go forth: APC is on the plough, and there is no looking back until Oshiomhole is sent back to the Senate in 2027. The task is not to boast of yesterday but to labour for tomorrow with humility, focus, and determination. The harvest belongs to those who keep ploughing. nigeria.title: A Ballot on a Burial Date? Northern Nigeria Confronts the Symbolism of January 16
nigeria.description: By Hassan A Karofi The choice of dates in politics is often presented as a matter of administrative convenience. Yet history teaches us that dates carry powerful symbolism, especially in societies where collective memories of tragedy and triumph remain deeply rooted. As Nigeria prepares for a presidential election scheduled for January 16, 2026, it is important to reflect on what that date means to millions of people, particularly in Northern Nigeria, where January 16 is associated with one of the darkest episodes in the country’s history. The significance of January 16 cannot be understood without revisiting the events of the country’s first military coup. In the early hours of January 15, 1966, a group of young military officers launched Nigeria’s first coup d’état. By the morning of January 16, the consequences of the coup were evident. Several of Nigeria’s most prominent political and military leaders had been assassinated. Among those killed were Sir Ahmadu Bello, the Sardauna of Sokoto and Premier of Northern Nigeria; Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, Nigeria’s first Prime Minister; Brigadier Samuel Ademulegun; Brigadier Zakariya Maimalari; and other senior political and military figures. While leaders from different regions were affected, the perception in the North was that the coup disproportionately targeted Northern political leadership. This perception would profoundly shape political attitudes and inter-ethnic relations for decades. The events following the coup further deepened Northern grievances. Major General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi assumed power and suspended parts of the constitutional order. In many parts of Northern Nigeria, suspicion and anger grew rapidly, culminating in the counter-coup of July 1966. The resulting instability ultimately contributed to the chain of events that led to the Nigerian Civil War. More than six decades later, the memory of January 1966 remains alive. For many Northern families, historians, traditional institutions, and political observers, January 16 is not merely another date on the calendar. It is a reminder of a traumatic turning point that altered Nigeria’s political trajectory and claimed the lives of leaders who continue to be revered across the region. Against this backdrop, the decision to hold a presidential election on January 16 raises legitimate questions. Whether the date was chosen for logistical, constitutional, or electoral reasons, policymakers should recognize that symbolism matters in politics. Elections are national events meant to unite citizens around a shared democratic purpose. When an election coincides with a date associated with historical mourning for a significant section of the country, there is a risk that the symbolism overshadows the democratic exercise itself. nigeria.title: One dead, five injured in clash at Asaba political rally
nigeria.description: One person has been killed and five others injured in a violent clash during a political rally organised by the Obedient/OK Movement in support of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Asaba, Delta State. The incident occurred at about 12:15 p.m. on Saturday, 7 November 2026, along Nnebisi Road in Asaba. The identities of the victims are yet to be established. According to a statement by the Delta State Police Command, the police had received an intelligence report indicating the likelihood of violence and invited the organisers to a security meeting. “During the engagement, they were briefed on the identified security threats and advised against holding an open road procession. They were further encouraged to conduct their political activities at a designated venue where appropriate security will be provided for them. However, the organisers ignored this important security advice and proceeded with the road procession,” the statement said. Upon receiving a distress call, police operatives mobilised to the scene and took the injured victims to the hospital for medical attention. Security was subsequently reinforced in the affected area to forestall further breakdown of law and order, while investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. Commissioner of Police Samuel E. Erale condemned the violence and reiterated that political parties are free to conduct lawful campaigns and other political activities. “He, however, advises all political parties and their supporters to avoid road processions in the interest of public safety and to liaise with the Police ahead of any political gatherings to facilitate adequate security arrangements,” the statement said. The CP assured residents of Delta State of the Command’s commitment to a thorough and impartial investigation and urge anyone with useful information to contact the Command through the following phone numbers; 09155570008 or 09155570007. nigeria.title: Real Madrid beat Valencia to level Liga leaders Barca
nigeria.description: Kylian Mbappe scored for the seventh match running as Real Madrid pulled provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a 3-0 win at 10-man Valencia on Saturday. Reigning champions Barca visit Atletico Madrid, third, on Sunday, aiming to move back clear of the chasing pack. Jose Mourinho’s Madrid largely dominated at Mestalla stadium as they secured an eighth win in a row across all competitions. Federico Valverde and Arda Guler’s first half goals put Madrid in the driving seat and Mbappe added a third in the second half. Los Blancos were without winger Vinicius Junior, who was serving the final game of a four-match ban. Madrid have thrived in his absence, putting heavy pressure on Barca, whom they beat in the Camp Nou Clasico on October 25. In the ninth minutes the match stopped for players and fans to pay tribute to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who tragically died on Tuesday. Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made a smart save to deny Aaron Mayol, who had picked Aurelien Tchouameni’s pocket in a dangerous area. Valencia’s Guido Rodriguez had a goal disallowed for offside before Mourinho’s side took control. Valverde drilled Madrid ahead from outside the area after Mbappe’s free-kick was blocked by the Valencia wall and fell to the Uruguayan. Guler soon doubled the lead, after Jude Bellingham’s cross was deflected kindly into his path. Guler had a good chance for the third in early in the second half but Valencia goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski grabbed the ball as the midfielder tried to round him. Minutes later Dimitrievski saved well from Mbappe as the French striker ran through and tried to dink the ball over him. Bellingham powered his way through the defence and was also denied by the goalkeeper, as was Mbappe following up with an overhead kick, as Madrid tried to find a third to kill off the game. Eventually Mbappe produced it, bursting onto a dangerous pass by Guler to dart past Dimitrievski and squeeze home his 13th league goal of the campaign. It was the forward’s 17th goal in 16 games across all competitions. Mbappe has netted in his last seven appearances for Madrid. Valencia’s Jose Gaya was dismissed with around 10 minutes remaining for a late sliding foul on Mbappe to further spoil Javier Aguirre’s team’s night. Earlier new Espanyol coach Eder Sarabia’s side were held to a goalless home draw by Deportivo La Coruna. Osasuna snatched a late 1-1 draw against Athletic Bilbao, while Racing Santander came from behind to beat Malaga 2-1. nigeria.title: Gas transportation network not responsible for power generation drop – NNPC
nigeria.description: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) has said its gas transportation network remains available to supply gas to power generating stations nationwide, insisting that transportation constraints are not responsible for the current decline in electricity generation. The national oil company said operational records of its subsidiary, NNPC Gas Infrastructure Company Limited (NGIC), showed no transportation-related constraints within its network that could explain the drop in power generation. NNPC disclosed this in a statement issued by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, in Abuja on Friday. The clarification followed a November 5 statement by the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), which attributed the decline in electricity generation partly to limited gas availability and reduced water inflows into hydroelectric power stations. However, NNPC said its clarification was specifically about the operational status of its gas transportation infrastructure, noting that gas production, commercial supply arrangements and actual deliveries to individual power plants were separate issues requiring independent assessment. The company said gas production had grown by about 10 per cent year-to-date in 2026, attributing the increase to the Federal Government’s gas development and monetisation agenda. “Gas supply availability is therefore not a challenge as NNPC remains committed to supporting efforts to improve electricity generation through safe, reliable and efficient gas supply and transportation,” the statement said. NNPC further explained that determining the causes of the generation shortfall required an assessment of other components of the gas-to-power value chain. These, it said, included the availability and operational readiness of generating units, plant maintenance schedules and actual gas offtake by power stations. The company stressed that the factors must be examined alongside gas supply data to establish the specific causes of the decline in electricity generation. It also called for a coordinated review of operational data by gas suppliers, transporters, power generators and NISO to identify constraints and guide appropriate interventions. NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to developing dependable energy infrastructure and collaborating with stakeholders to translate the country’s gas resources into more reliable electricity supply for Nigerians. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi

I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. A critical part of thriving through a transition, a pivot or when you are starting over is to be honest about your limits. These could be the limits of your existing knowledge, expertise, and others. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. entertainment.title: Africa Comedy Live Brings Its Platform to Africa, Opening With an Invitation-Only Founding Gathering in Lagos
entertainment.description: Africa Comedy Live (ACL), the platform connecting African comedians, content creators and audiences across the continent and the diaspora, today announces its arrival in Africa with an invitation-only founding gathering, A Salute to Nollywood, to be held on Friday, 13 November 2026 at TRIB3 , Victoria Island, Lagos. The evening marks two milestones at once: the introduction of the Africa Comedy Live platform to the African market, and a formal salute to the comedians and storytellers whose work built the audience that African comedy now commands. Africa Comedy Live has been presenting African comedy live in the United States since 2019, with artists including Kenny Blaq , Helen Paul , Real Warri Pikin and David Operah . The platform, live at www.africacomedylive.com, is another channel, not a replacement for the ones creators already use. It allows creators to keep the audiences they have already built, earn more, and expand opportunities across continents, while giving viewers across Africa and the diaspora a single place to discover the comedians and creators worth following. A Salute to Nollywood brings together comedians, entertainment professionals, media and prospective partners for an evening built around three things: an introduction to the platform through a live demonstration, a celebration of African comedy, and a salute to the generation of performers whose influence continues to shape new talent. “Africa’s comedy has never lacked talent. What it has lacked is a stage that belongs to it,” said Carrie Crawford, Founder of Africa Comedy Live. “For seven years we have put African comedians in front of live audiences in the United States. Now we are bringing that home. Africa Comedy Live is that permanent stage, and Lagos is where it begins,” He added. The gathering is by invitation only and is not open to public attendance. For comedy lovers, the evening is an introduction to the platform and a way to follow the journey. For creators, it is an opportunity to express interest in joining the community. For brands and partners, it is a chance to explore ways to support African comedy’s next chapter. ABOUT AFRICA COMEDY LIVE Africa Comedy Live is a web platform connecting African comedians, content creators and brands across the continent and the diaspora. Founded by Carrie Crawford, ACL has presented African comedy live in the United States since 2019 and is built on a simple conviction: Africa’s comedy deserves a world stage, and a place to call home. entertainment.title: iDICE Named Official Deal Room Partner for Afreximbank’s CANEX WKND 2026
entertainment.description: The Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Programme, a US$617 million initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), will take part in Afreximbank’s Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND 2026) as one of the event’s official Deal Room Partner. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. The Eagles put together a seven-play, 75-yard drive that Jones finished with a 7-yard keeper, cutting the deficit to 28-23 with more than 11 minutes left to play. The ending turned on two late fumbles and a missed kick. Gino Addison, who ran for a game-high 174 yards on 18 carries, fumbled, and Norfolk State recovered with 1:27 remaining. Quarterback Deljay Bailey then ran for 13 yards but fumbled it right back to Central. Jones found Wall for the 26-yard touchdown that put the Eagles ahead 29-28 with 27 seconds left. Norfolk State still had a chance. After an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty on North Carolina Central, the Spartans moved into range, and Marco Peery lined up for a 37-yard field goal attempt with four seconds left that missed. sports.description: SEATTLE − Legendary Penn State football player and longtime radio broadcaster Jack Ham was in stable condition in the University of Washington Medical Center Saturday evening, Nov. 7, according to university officials, after undergoing a medical emergency here before the Nittany Lions ' game. Ham, 77, was rushed to the hospital an hour or so before Penn State began their eventual 28-25 victory here in Husky Stadium. After the game, head coach Matt Campbell began his press conference by addressing Ham − and the apparent efforts to help him to safety and a hopeful recovery from his an undisclosed medical situation. Campbell singled out longtime radio partner and play-by-play announcer Steve Jones, who apparently was by Ham's side when he fell ill. The Lions (5-4, 2-4 Big Ten) held on to beat Washington with a dramatic save at the end. "Everybody knows that man, this was a gut-wrenching day for Penn State football with Jack Ham,” Campbell said. “Obviously, a really tough situation as we got off the buses here (at the stadium). “First of all, I think we should all know Steve Jones and the heroic effort that he did for somebody he loves dearly. And if it’s not for Steve, you know, and what he did, I don’t know if we would have as good a news as we do right now. And then I want to also thank the University of Washington, their athletic director, their emergency team were incredible. They were outstanding. I think, hopefully, as all of you know, Jack is in stable condition right now, and obviously, the emotion of that." Penn State went on to play their best first half of football of the season in leading the Huskies 28-6 at halftime − before holding off a second-half surge and desperately hanging on. “What I was really proud of our football team, and we talked about a little bit before we went out to the game," Campbell said. "Just the courage of our kids to play with what Jack Ham means to Penn State football, how that guy played the game, how that guy still to this day serves our football program. It was awesome to be able to go win the football game for him and his family, and our thoughts and prayers will continue to be with him on a full recovery.” Penn State officials were not disclosing the nature of Ham's medical issue or any further details yet on his condition. The Johnstown, Pa. native has worked for more than two decades with Jones, the pair calling their 300th game in 2023. Ham was a consensus All-American linebacker at Penn State and the 34th player taken in the 1971 NFL Draft. He would go on to win four Super Bowls with the Pittsburgh Steelers and would be regarded as one of the best linebackers in NFL history with a particular supremacy as a pass defender. Ham was named the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year in 1975 and made eight straight Pro Bowls. Frank Bodani covers Penn State football for the York Daily Record and USA Today Network. sports.description: They sweated it out in the end, but the Nittany Lions were able to pull out a victory over the Washington Huskies 28-25. Carson Hansen and Chase Sowell starred in an electrifying first half display where the Nittany Lions had 303 total yards, more than they ha in Big Ten games this season. Still, there was a worrying comeback attempt that exposed the defensive frailties that occurred pre-bye week. That's why this game wasn't perfect. Still, the Nittany Lions come away with a second straight Big Ten win and is looking like they could potentially contend for bowl eligibility. Here is a look at the postgame report card for the Nittany Lions against Washington. Quarterback: B For some reason, Rocco Becht can never have a complete Big Ten performance. In the first half of the game, Becht was 11 of 17 for 193 yards and 2 touchdowns. His chemistry with both Zay Robinson and Chase Sowell was on point and it allowed the Nittany Lions to score with ease on four of six first half possessions. Then the second half came. He only completed five passes for 47 yards and didn't lead a single scoring drive. Had the Nittany Lions blown this lead, he probably wouldn't have heard the end of it from fans. Still, he did enough to win and did not turn the ball over, albeit with a couple nervy moments sprinkled in. Running Backs: B+ This was more of an efficient rather than an explosive performance by the Penn State running backs. Unlike last week, they were held under 200 yards and it was a similar committee approach. As predicted, Carson Hansen shown early and was the leading rusher for the squad with 119 yards on 14 carries and a 12 yard touchdown. Meanwhile, Cam Wallace had the other rushing touchdown on the day and finished with 56 yards. Still, it's nice to know that a player of Sowell's caliber can carry the weight for a Jekyll and Hyde offense. sports.title: Mike Florio plans to ‘ignore’ Dianna Russini’s reporting at Pro Football Talk until ‘credibility is somehow restored’
sports.description: Credit: PFT Live; The Rich Eisen Show All signs are pointing toward Dianna Russini returning to NFL media next week with a new weekly podcast. The question now is what form her content will take. Will Russini attempt to slide back into her role as an insider? Is her plan to continue to break news? And most importantly, will she address her alleged affair with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel? As the leader of one of the most important platforms in the NFL, Mike Florio is pushing publicly for these answers. Florio not only hosts PFT Live for NBC Sports and contributes to Football Night In America , but he also runs Pro Football Talk, the news site that aggregates all of the league’s latest news and rumors in one place and is widely read by fans and industry insiders. In the latest episode of PFT Live , Florio stated that he plans to “ignore” any news from Russini “unless the credibility is somehow restored.” As Florio sees it, the starting point is that Russini must address what happened with Vrabel. Florio noted that so far, Russini’s only two public comments on the matter were both denials. In the initial article that broke the story open at the New York Post , Russini denied she had any relationship with Vrabel. When she resigned from The Athletic, she accused the media of stretching the truth. “If there’s going to be actual reporting as part of this, you’ve gotta have some credibility, or nobody’s going to believe what you say,” Florio said. “Is there going to be an effort to be an insider again? Unless and until we get an explanation that restores credibility… as somebody who aggregates the reports of others, amplifies the reports of others, wants my audience to believe the reporting of others, I’ve gotta believe it first. “And after everything that’s happened, everything we know, I’m not going to be inclined to believe anything. Which means I’m not going to be amplifying anything. I don’t care what the reporting is. Unless and until it’s confirmed by someone who doesn’t have these credibility issues, I’m going to ignore it. Unless the credibility is somehow restored.” Russini appears to be partnering with BetUS on the weekly show, as well as a written column. She reportedly hired a crisis publicist to help with her return. In an internal report at The Athletic released earlier this year , the outlet’s standards editor stated that Russini’s relationship was a “violation” of standards. The editor found multiple instances of improper attribution of information related to Vrabel and his teams, as well as a video interview that called into question how Russini got access to the head coach. After the report was released, Russini gave a statement saying she stood by her reporting . It would be hard to imagine Russini returning to the public eye without addressing the situation in some way, but news writers and commentators like Florio are already making it clear she will have to earn back trust beyond a simple statement. Applications are now open for the agency’s next class of astronauts, who will join NASA as America returns to the Moon, builds the Moon Base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars. The next generation of astronauts will train to operate on the lunar surface, live and work beyond Earth, and take on missions that will push the boundaries of human exploration farther than ever before. Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage. NASA’s astronaut corps has always called on remarkable Americans willing to take on extraordinary challenges in service to the nation. If you are ready to join that tradition, come help write the next chapter of humanity’s greatest adventure.” NASA expects to make its final selection in late 2027 to begin training as the next class of astronaut candidates. “The window is open. The mission is waiting. And the only thing missing from the greatest adventure humanity has ever embarked upon is you,” said NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." science.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
science.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . science.description: null SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U.S. military. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base this evening (Nov. 6) at 7:48 p.m. EST (4:48 p.m. local California time; 0048 GMT on Nov. 7), rising into the sky as the sun sank toward the Pacific. The launch kicked off the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force , which we know little about. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) That touchdown occurred aboard the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange in the Pacific Ocean. It wrapped up the eighth flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1095. The Falcon 9's upper stage, meanwhile, continued carrying its mystery payload skyward. It could be headed to low Earth orbit , outside observers speculate. "It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites for the USSF's Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio based on SpaceX's Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches," NextSpaceflight.com wrote in a mission description . Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites. Starshield is a similar system designed to provide services to the U.S. military and its allies. Starshield satellites are believed to be based heavily on the Starlink spacecraft bus. (Image credit: SpaceX) Previous Booster 1095 missions GPS-III 8 | 6 Starlink missions USSF-432 was the 119th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, and the 14th national-security flight of the rocket so far this year. The vast majority of Falcon 9 missions in 2026 — more than 70% — have been devoted to building out the Starlink megaconstellation. SpaceX has also launched six other missions this year. Three were operational flights of the company's Falcon Heavy rocket, while the other three were test missions of its next-gen Starship vehicle. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
science.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus. science.title: Record-breaking, fast-spinning magnet could help uncover new physics
science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. science.title: An unexpected feedback loop may be driving mega heatwaves
science.description: Land scorched by a fire in Wennington, London, during the record-breaking heatwave in 2022 Shutterstock Mid-latitude regions such as Europe are set to suffer more intense heatwaves than previously thought, according to new research that has uncovered a three-way feedback loop that amplifies extreme heat conditions. Heatwaves across the world have shocked scientists with their scale and severity in recent years, with heat extremes dramatically outstripping both historical records and the predictions of climate models. Read more Extreme heat is now making cities unlivable. How can we survive it? In the UK in 2022, temperatures exceeded 40°C (104 ° F) for the first time in history, despite predictions that such a milestone was probably still years away. Likewise, the 2021 heatwave in the Pacific Northwest saw temperatures hit extremes that far outstripped climate model projections. Advertisement Researchers have been scrambling to understand why very extreme heat is occurring more frequently, and with greater intensity, than expected at this level of warming. One team thinks the answer lies partly in the soil. Scientists already knew that high-pressure systems allow more solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface, heating up the land. They also knew that higher temperatures dry soils more quickly, removing the cooling effect provided by evaporation, thereby further amplifying heatwaves. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Now it seems that when temperatures climb high enough, dry soil, high pressure and extreme heat can amplify each other further, with dry soil helping to sustain high-pressure systems in the atmosphere. “Basically, the soils that are affected by circulation pattern also start to affect back on the circulation pattern itself,” says Kai Kornhuber at the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis in Austria. This three-way feedback effect makes extreme heatwaves 10 per cent hotter than they would otherwise be, according to the research by Kornhuber and his colleagues – a factor not fully accounted for in climate model projections. This will have serious consequences for our ability to cope with future extreme heat. “Ten per cent hotter or colder can really make a difference between a heatwave and a record-shattering heatwave,” says Kornhuber. “We’re facing so many critical thresholds in social and biophysical systems that an extra 10 per cent can really lead to temperatures that are then quite damaging.” Read more Is a broken jet stream causing extreme weather that lasts longer? science.title: See the space race like you’ve never seen it before in PBS’s new living documentary, ‘We Chose to Go to the Moon’
science.description: null Straight from its inspiring live performance at New York City's Carnegie Hall this past April, RadicalMedia's filmed presentation of the immersive living space documentary, "We Chose to Go to the Moon," is finally available for the rest of us to watch. "We Chose to Go to the Moon" premieres Nov. 10 at 8:00 p.m. ET on PBS, PBS.org, and the PBS app, and we’ve got an exclusive clip to share featuring Mark and Kali Armstrong singing "Flight of Fancy." With a poignant introduction by Oscar winning director Ron Howard ("Apollo 13"), "We Chose to Go to the Moon" recalls the extraordinary saga of the global space race and Apollo moon landings by actors portraying pivotal persons who made it all happen. These roles include astronauts Neil Armstrong , Buzz Aldrin, Michael Collins and Ed White, Mission Control trailblazer Poppy Northcutt, " Hidden Figures " mathematician Katherine Johnson and members of the spacefaring families that remained on Earth, including Janet Armstrong and Betty Grissom. This dynamic multimedia production is directed by Tony Award winner Michael Mayer ("Chess"), combining a unique fusion of theater, concert and documentary storytelling using rare archival footage alongside historic flags and artifacts taken to the Moon and returned home. It also revisits the ill-fated Apollo 13 mission and adds a special tribute to moonwalker Neil Armstrong performed by his son Mark and granddaughter Kali. "We Chose to Go to the Moon" is created, written and narrated by historian John Monsky and stars Ian Weinberger ("Hamilton"), Skylar Astin ("Pitch Perfect"), Brent Comer ("The Outsiders"), Claybourne Elder ("Company"), Elizabeth Gillies (Netflix's "Dynasty"), Taylor Louderman ("Mean Girls") and Joy Woods ("Galileo").
